autonomousPushReason: Pushing to main triggers .github/workflows/build-image.yml, which publishes a multi-arch container image to GHCR tagged 0.10.0 and latest.

findings.title: Tunnel route guard bypassed by percent-encoding, exposing the admin API and password login to the internet
findings.summary: The guard that keeps the admin panel LAN-only compared the RAW url against '/api/', but Fastify's router percent-decodes path segments before matching. '/kiosk/%61pi/admin/plans' reached the real admin route (401) where '/kiosk/api/admin/plans' was correctly refused (404), and '/kiosk/%61pi/login' reached the real password login. Confirmed live against a running server. requireAdmin still failed closed, so no donor data was readable without a session.

findings.title: @fastify/static 8.3.0 carries four high advisories including authorization bypass on non-canonical paths
findings.summary: GHSA-8pvw-jcv7-9cmj, GHSA-x428-ghpx-8j92, GHSA-83w8-p2f5-377r, GHSA-pr96-94w5-mx2h. Reachable: the plugin is mounted on /uploads/ (admin-uploaded images, public) and on the built web app. Two of the four are the same class of route-guard bypass this repo demonstrated in KIOSK-001. Fixed by a major upgrade to 10.1.2, verified against a running server.

findings.title: No audit trail for admin actions that cancel, pause or reschedule a donor's recurring plan
findings.summary: The three plan write routes stop or alter a real donor's standing order and recorded nothing on success. A masjid's admin login is shared in practice and Stripe's dashboard only ever says 'cancelled by API key', so there was no way to reconstruct who did what. Added an append-only admin_audit table, writes from plan cancel/pause/schedule plus device revoke and PIN rotation, and a read-only GET /api/admin/audit.

findings.title: Keyed-card WebView follows any top-level navigation (kiosk escape surface)
findings.summary: The WebViewClient overrode only shouldInterceptRequest, so a top-level navigation would turn a full-screen donor-facing WebView inside a locked kiosk into an unrestricted browser. No live path reaches it (kioskpay.html makes no top-level navigation; 3DS renders in an iframe), so this is defence in depth. Fixed with a main-frame-only allowlist; sub-frames left unrestricted so 3-D Secure keeps working.

findings.title: Pairing-code brute force limited per peer only, with no global budget
findings.summary: A 6-digit single-use code with a per-peer limiter that grants 5 free attempts per source address. An attacker with many addresses (a /64 of IPv6 on a LAN) multiplies free guesses while no bucket trips. A guessed code mints a device token, which can pull the kiosk config containing the exit-PIN hash. Added a shared budget of 50 failures per 10 minutes across all peers.

findings.title: GitHub Actions on mutable tags in the job that holds the APK signing keystore
findings.summary: Nine action references on floating tags, including third-party android-actions/setup-android@v3, in a job that decodes the APK signing keystore to disk. A repointed tag takes the keystore and with it the ability to publish a signed kiosk update every paired tablet accepts. All pinned to commit SHAs resolved and verified via the GitHub API.

findings.title: Exit-PIN backoff overflows to a negative duration and restarts its ramp
findings.summary: Unbounded attempts fed the shift distance directly; JVM lshl masks it to 6 bits and wraps on overflow, so attempt 64 yields a negative lockout and attempt 67 restarts the ramp at 5s. Initially rated High on the assumption the throttle collapsed; measurement shows 13.5 guesses/hour against an intended 12.0, and a 4-digit PIN still needs ~31 days of continuous attack. Re-rated Low. Fixed by clamping steps before the shift, which is observably identical in the intended range.

findings.title: Transitive dependency vulnerabilities in fast-uri, find-my-way, brace-expansion and postcss
findings.summary: Four upstream-high advisories, none attacker-reachable here: find-my-way's needs HTTP/2 which this server does not serve, fast-uri is used by Ajv for schema $id resolution not user URLs, postcss is build-time only. Cleared with a non-breaking npm audit fix in both packages; server 4 high to 0, web 1 high to 0.

findings.title: LoginLimiter never evicts throttled entries, so the map grows without bound
findings.summary: The sweep required fails <= MAX_FREE, a condition only entries that had never been throttled can satisfy, so precisely the entries consuming memory were kept for the life of the process. Now evicts any lapsed entry, with a test asserting an actively-throttled peer is not swept early.

findings.title: No X-Content-Type-Options or Referrer-Policy on any response
findings.summary: nosniff matters most on /uploads/*, where admin-uploaded files are served: it stops a browser reinterpreting a 'PNG' whose bytes begin with markup. A framing header was deliberately omitted pending confirmation of whether OpenMasjidOS iframes installed apps.

findings.title: ScryptPin accepts an unbounded scrypt cost from synced config
findings.summary: N was floored at 2 with no ceiling, so a corrupt or hostile config would provoke a huge allocation at the PIN pad; the resulting OutOfMemoryError is an Error, not an Exception, so it would bypass the catch below and crash a locked kiosk instead of failing closed. Bounded to the server's own 64 MiB maxmem.

findings.title: HTTPS-upgrade redirect port is influenced by an untrusted X-Forwarded-Host header
findings.summary: lastHttpsHost is learned from x-forwarded-host with trustProxy off. hostOnly() strips the port when comparing, so a LAN attacker can poison the redirect's PORT and send an admin browser to https://<same-host>:<attacker-port>/. Deferred: every candidate fix needs knowledge of how the platform's TLS proxy sets Host vs X-Forwarded-Host, which cannot be observed without a live OpenMasjidOS, and shipping an unverified change to the redirect that serves the admin panel is the worse trade.

findings.title: Container runs as root
findings.summary: No USER directive. Deferred, not fixed: /data is a named volume whose kiosk.db is root-owned at 0600 on every existing install, so USER node would break the whole deployed fleet on update, and cap_drop ALL removes CAP_CHOWN/CAP_SETUID so an entrypoint drop-privileges pattern cannot work either. Mitigated in practice by the container already running with no capabilities and no-new-privileges. Needs a coordinated image + compose + volume-chown migration.

findings.title: Donation totals treat UTC midnight as the start of the masjid's day
findings.summary: No TZ is set in the Dockerfile or compose, so 'today', 'this week' and 'this month' are UTC windows. A masjid in California sees today's total reset at 5pm local. The conversion code is correct; it simply has no idea where the masjid is. Deferred: fixing it properly needs a masjid timezone setting plus UI, which is a feature, and guessing a timezone produces quietly wrong numbers.

findings.title: consumeTuitionSession is dead code and its comment asserts a property the code lacks
findings.summary: Exported and never called. Its doc comment says a tuition session is single-use for the pay step; in fact a session survives its 15-minute TTL and can mint several PaymentIntents. Not a vulnerability (every mint recomputes the amount server-side and re-checks the device binding, and re-minting is useful after a declined card), but a comment asserting a security property that does not hold. Deferred: deleting versus wiring it up is a product decision.

findings.title: No Android unit tests exist, so pure security-relevant functions are untestable
findings.summary: KioskViewModel.backoffUntil and ScryptPin.verify are pure functions guarding a public terminal and neither can be tested today; a JVM test source set would have caught KIOSK-002 outright. Deferred: adding test infrastructure is beyond an audit's remit and cannot be validated on a machine with no Android SDK.
